_README: HUMAN-ENTERED SOURCE VALUES for the DC-URS socio-economic pillar.
This file is edited by a person, not written by a script, and that is deliberate.
Every automated route was tested and none is usable:
- WorldPop gridded age structure: 1.5 GB per band x 12 bands, server rejects range reads
- NFHS-5 state report FR374: a HEALTH survey — carries no 65+ population share and no
slum variable. Verified by reading the report, not assumed.
- census2011.co.in: returned HUGLI district data for a Kolkata URL and described Hooghly
as part of Maharashtra. Factually wrong; unusable.
- censusindia.gov.in: authoritative, but tables are XLSX/PDF behind navigation.
So each number below is transcribed by hand from a primary source and carries its own
citation. fetch-socio.py validates them and computes the composite; it does not invent them.
A value left null blocks that ward, loudly — it never silently becomes zero.
age structure + informal settlement  <- Census of India 2011 (the only instrument that
measures them; no newer census exists — the 2021
Both vintages are displayed on the tool. Do not average them into one date.

census2011._source: Census of India 2011, District Census Handbook, South Twenty Four Parganas

nfhs5._source: NFHS-5 (2019-21) District Fact Sheet, South Twenty Four Parganas, West Bengal

census2011._source: Census of India 2011, District Census Handbook, North Twenty Four Parganas

_where_to_get_them.census2011: censusindia.gov.in -> Census Tables -> 2011 -> West Bengal -> District Census Handbook. Table C-13 gives single-year age; Table A-2 gives slum population. Alternatively the DCHB district PDF, Primary Census Abstract.
_where_to_get_them.nfhs5: rchiips.org/nfhs -> NFHS-5 -> District Fact Sheets -> West Bengal. Two pages per district. (This host blocks some networks; reachable from India.)
